gaps.sentence: You ___ have worried — everything turned out fine.
gaps.hint: the worry was unnecessary in the end
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have' means the action happened but was unnecessary: needn't have.

gaps.sentence: When the lift broke, I ___ walk up ten flights of stairs.
gaps.hint: necessity created by a past event
gaps.explanation: 'Had to' expresses past necessity: had to walk.

gaps.sentence: You ___ have seen her face when she heard the news!
gaps.explanation: 'Should have seen' emphasizes how remarkable something was: should have.

gaps.sentence: She ___ have received your email — her inbox was full last week.
gaps.hint: ruled out as a past possibility
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' plus the participle rules out a past possibility: can't have received.

gaps.sentence: I didn't ___ to like coffee, but now I drink it every day.
gaps.hint: negative of used to, spelled use
gaps.explanation: In the negative, 'used to' becomes 'didn't use to': use.

gaps.sentence: Candidates ___ switch off their phones before the exam begins.
You ___ to apply for a visa before you travel; the airline will check it.
gaps.explanation: 'Need to' expresses necessity and, unlike 'must', takes 'to': need to apply.

gaps.sentence: I ___ help thinking he is hiding something.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't help' plus -ing means being unable to stop a feeling: can't help thinking.
